highlights.title: A Georgia Cop Used Flock to Track 2 Other Cops: His Ex and Her Friend
highlights.summary: After an affair with a fellow police officer ended, a Georgia cop used Flock to track her movements—and those of a man whose vehicle often showed up near hers, internal investigation records show.
body: In recent months, there has been a surge in reports of police officers misusing automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) sold by Flock Safety to stalk former romantic partners—but details about these incidents are often scarce.
Now, with documents obtained via a public records request, WIRED can reveal specific details about one extensive Flock-fueled surveillance campaign and the subsequent investigation and fallout.

Dustin Bozzo, who until this month worked as a patrolman in the Atlanta-area suburb of Alpharetta, Georgia, allegedly used Flock 56 times between March and May to search for the license plate of a former romantic partner—a fellow member of the Alpharetta Police Department. (Their relationship itself violated the city’s ban on workplace dating, documents show.) When Bozzo noticed that his ex’s car was often near that of another police officer, he began searching for that officer’s vehicle as well. He did so 29 times between March and May.

highlights.title: This Is How Anthropic Thinks AI Agents Should Navigate the Physical World
highlights.summary: The potential for AI to automate scientific research and manufacturing must be balanced with new risks, Anthropic says.
body: Artificial intelligence agents might occasionally get confused and hack into other computers, but Anthropic thinks it has a way to unleash the little rascals into scientific labs and manufacturing facilities safely.

The AI company released details today of a new framework designed to help AI agents use physical systems like microscopes, liquid-handling equipment, quantum computing hardware, manufacturing machines, and robot arms.

The framework, called Model Hardware Standard, is a set of rules that specify how AI agents should—and should not—interact with all sorts of hardware. It reflects a growing belief that AI has the potential to revolutionize scientific research and industries like manufacturing–if it can venture into the physical world safely.

The company says it will work with trusted partners to determine how to maximize safety before making it generally available. Though there are potential misuse issues involved—developing biological weapons, for instance—the company says guardrails built into AI models themselves should prevent bad actors from taking advantage of the new standard for nefarious ends.

highlights.title: 'Forza Horizon 6' Reportedly Delayed for PS5 as Console Wars Heat Up
highlights.summary: After a brief armistice, the console wars are back on. Despite an earlier announcement that Xbox's Forza Horizon 6 would come to PlayStation 5 sometime this year, it seems the port has been quietly delayed. The Verge’s Tom Warren wrote as much on X, with IGN affirming the claim.
body: Forza Horizon 6 ’s 2026 release window for PS5 was announced shortly before the game came out on PC and Xbox Series X|S to glowing praise. However, things have changed at Xbox since earlier this year. Asha Sharma took over as Xbox Game Division CEO back in February, while several members of executive leadership left the company. Sharma later announced that Xbox would be undergoing a major “reset” to address its recent financial struggles. This culminated in a July announcement that 3,200 employees would be laid off over the next fiscal quarter and that Microsoft would be cutting ties with several of its studios.

Around the same time, Microsoft began to deemphasize publishing its games on rival platforms. While Halo: Campaign Evolved was released on PlayStation 5, Xbox reportedly pulled the game's trailer from one of Sony's State of Play broadcasts. Xbox also reportedly killed a mostly complete PS5 port of Gears of War: E-Day shortly before its reveal.

highlights.summary: Hugging Face's Pollen Robotics has launched its second cute AI robot, the Microduck, a one-eyed biped standing just under 10 inches tall. It's available to preorder now for $399 in cream, graphite, lavender, and sky blue, and Pollen Robotics says it plans to start shipping the little robot "before…
body: Video demos of the Microduck show it picking up socks and markers, kicking around a ball, and zipping around on tiny rollerskates. Pollen Robotics says it can also “react to its surroundings” and follow around a laser pointer, or users can control it with a game controller. The Microduck’s software is open-source, like Hugging Face’s previous Reachy Mini robot, so users can also retrain it to do new tricks.

The Microduck can sing, too, and Pollen Robotics says each one has its own sound: “it communicates through weird little sounds, closer to a creature than an assistant. Each Microduck gets its own audio identity the first time it wakes up, tied to that individual robot so it keeps the same voice for life.” It runs on a Rockchip RK3566 processor and has a camera, motion sensors, LiDAR, and articulated legs, head, and neck.

highlights.title: England on back foot as Pakistan's bowlers shine at gloomy Lord's
highlights.summary: Mohammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali starred with the ball as Pakistan took advantage of overcast conditions at Lord's to reduce England to 248-9 on day one of the second Test.
body: A deluge of rain had postponed play until 12.20pm on Thursday afternoon, and much like the weather, England's day got off to a dreary start, with the hosts going 3-36 after just 10.3 overs.

After a week dominated by England's latest off-field incident involving bowler Brydon Carse, captain Joe Root's mood would not have lifted much as he was dismissed on Thursday by Abbas for just four runs.
That was further compounded by the cheap dismissals of Ben Duckett (17) and Emilio Gay (8), who were also snared by Abbas.
As the weather improved, England rallied with Jordan Cox bringing up a score of 55 off 105 deliveries and combined well with Jamie Smith, making a partnership of 67 off 97 deliveries.

highlights.title: The LEGO Mario Minifigure Sets Look Like a Much-Needed ‘Reset’ for the Mario Theme
highlights.summary: LEGO has announced its first sets based around a new group of Mario minifigures, and they look pretty great. The company has just released pictures of the boxes these sets will come in, and, uh, I kind of want these sets just for the boxes?
body: The boxes are bright and bold and colorful, all decked out in the same red and blue shades that make Mario the recognizable mascot as he is. I mean, just look at this box for the Fire Mario & Bower’s Castle set. It’s perfect.

This new line of Mario sets is something of a reset ( ba-dum-tss ) for the LEGO Mario theme. Mario and LEGO have years of history together, including plenty of awesome Nintendo LEGO sets. But the overwhelming majority of the Mario sets belonged to a play-focused LEGO Super Mario theme.

These sets were based around a big (for LEGO), boxy, non-minifigure Mario that could “interact” with the environmental elements you built. That interaction was limited to sounds and music coming out of the Mario figure, along with simple animations that played on a tiny LED screen built into his chest.

I got to try out a handful of these sets when LEGO added a boxy Luigi figure to the mix. Let’s just say they didn’t wow me. They were clearly designed for young kids, but I had young kids at the time, and they didn’t want to play with the sets for more than a couple minutes, either.

highlights.title: Like a rhinestone cowgirl – Dolly Parton’s most glorious, joyful and meta looks
highlights.summary: Across six decades, the late country singer and pop culture icon turned self‑presentation into a flamboyant art form. • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: Dolly Parton may have had a record 25 US country No 1 singles, released 66 studio albums and earned six Golden Globe nominations, among many other achievements, but the Tennessee-born star also had an incredible number of fashion moments. “It costs a lot of money to look this cheap”, she famously quipped when asked about her style. As we bid her farewell, six Guardian writers reflect on their favourite Dolly looks.

While Parton wore a plethora of looks, sometimes up to 10 a day, you always knew what you were going to get. For over 60 years she held firm to her signature style – a silhouette that emphasised her tiny waist, along with high heels, higher hair and a heavy sprinkling of sparkle. In today’s world of image architects and constant reinvention, her continuity felt even more refreshing.

highlights.title: The iconic T-38 jets flown by astronauts just got a spiffy new look
highlights.summary: For the first time in decades, NASA has rolled out one of its iconic astronaut training aircraft with a bold, new look. The space agency debuted a new livery on one of its T-38 jets in celebration of its program to return astronauts to the Moon.
body: “This new ‘Artemis’ livery has a black and white paint scheme with blue and red stripes that separate those two paint schemes,” said Sean Brady, who proposed and designed the new livery while serving as the T-38 project pilot in NASA’s Aircraft Operations Division (AOD), part of the Flight Operations Directorate at Johnson Space Center in Houston. “The Artemis program logo in the back and a picture of the Moon is on the left and right side of the rear fuselage.”

The Northrop T-38 “Talon” two-seat supersonic trainer has been in use by NASA since 1962, when the first jets were loaned to the agency by the US Air Force. Flown today to familiarize new astronauts with working in a high-stress, dynamic environment and maintain pilots’ flight proficiencies, Johnson Space Center currently has a fleet of 14 active T-38 jets stationed out of nearby Ellington Airport.
All but one is adorned with the classic blue stripe livery that has been associated with most of NASA’s aircraft over the past five decades.

highlights.title: Plaud is launching AI earbuds
highlights.summary: Plaud has introduced a new AI wearable that's designed to record, transcribe, and summarize your conversations, only this time it looks like earbuds instead of a pin. The Plaud One Explorer Edition can be worn like traditional earbuds or used through its standalone charging case, and the case…
body: Preorders are now available for the $249.99 Plaud One, with shipping to start in September.

Each earbud features 16MB of local storage (for a total of 32MB) and three microphones that can record at a distance of up to two meters. They can record for up to six hours according to Plaud, which is also the maximum estimated battery life. The earbuds also include noise cancellation features and force-activated sensor controls on the stem. The charging case includes four microphones with a five-meter recording range, a built-in speaker, 512MB of storage, and provides a combined battery life of up to 36 hours, which can be recharged via USB-C.

Plaud On’s AI transcription and summarization capabilities use Plaud Intelligence, which the company says is designed to “understand and execute on human intent.” An AI button on the Plaud One charging case can be used to activate “Plaud Agent,” which natively integrates with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, and Slack, to prevent users from having to switch between various platforms.
The Plaud One costs $249.99 and is available to preorder “in selected markets” starting today, with shipping expected to start in late September.

highlights.title: Playdate Manufacturer Panic Is Passing Tariff Refunds to Customers
highlights.summary: Panic's Playdate, a crank-powered handheld gaming system, launched all the way back in 2022, but last year it got hit with the same tariffs as many gaming products. Now that the Supreme Court has ordered the government to refund those fees, Panic is forwarding those refunds to the customers that…
body: The company started sending out emails, spotted on LinkedIn and Reddit, informing customers that they'd be getting a tariff refund sent to their original payment method. The refund itself isn't much — the highest one I've seen is a $25 refund — but when it's attached to a handheld that costs $250 now and $179 at launch, it's a pretty decent percentage.

If you bought one of these fun little handhelds when the tariffs were active, you should be automatically getting an email notifying you of the refund. If not, you should be able to reach out to help@play.date to figure out what's going on.

Ideally, we'd see more companies refunding tariffs now that the refunds have started flowing from the governmen, but there are definitely companies that are holding on to those fees. Even Nintendo has refused to issue refunds to Switch 2 customers, arguing that gamers got exactly what they paid for. Hopefully, the Playdate manufacturers can set a decent example for other companies to follow.

highlights.title: How do you define good health – and achieve it – in a broken US medical system?
highlights.summary: In a new book, Dr Lucy McBride aims to help us navigate US healthcare – and tread carefully in the wellness industry. Most of us want to be healthy, but it’s easier said than done. In the US, people are caught between a broken medical system and a well-resourced wellness industry.
body: Over 25 years of practicing medicine, running a primary care practice in Washington DC, Dr Lucy McBride has seen patients struggle to navigate the medical system.

In her new book, Beyond the Prescription, McBride presents a practical framework for getting the best results from a flawed system. It begins with defining what health means to you. For one person, it might be running ultramarathons and extending longevity at any cost; for another, it might be balance and the freedom to indulge.

“The relationship between a patient and their primary care doctor is, at its best, one of the most protective forces in human health – and, right now, we’re systematically dismantling it,” says McBride over Zoom.

It’s no wonder patients feel unheard, unsatisfied and lost. We spoke about how people can advocate for themselves and pursue their vision of health. Our conversation has been condensed and edited for clarity.

highlights.title: Netflix Failed at Video Games. Now It’s Trying to Promote Them
highlights.summary: Netflix has walked back plans to put AAA games on its streaming platform. Instead, it's pivoting to marketing highly anticipated titles like Grand Theft Auto VI.
body: Later today, Netflix will stream a live event with Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive, the developer and publisher of the highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto VI. Called Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look, it’s the third official trailer for the game, which releases on November 19.

This collaborative stunt follows a week of hacker leaks and gamer consternation on Rockstar’s decision not to ship the game with physical discs. The hackers initially said the leaks, which revealed GTA VI gameplay and story spoilers, were attempts to convince Rockstar to include physical discs. But the hackers quickly pivoted to collecting cryptocurrency in exchange for more leaks. Rockstar shared a statement on X saying the leaks had been “heartbreaking” for the team. It also wrote that the company is “excited for everyone to see the extended look.”

highlights.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
highlights.summary: Some of the world's largest tech companies and AI startups have come together to decry the current state of cybersecurity and to advertise a new solution that they say can ward off a new generation of cyber threats.
body: Over a hundred tech companies — including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft — have signed an open letter urging both the private and public sectors to work together to defend themselves from AI-related cyber threats.

The letter — which was also signed by prominent cyber firms like Crowdstrike, Okta, and Fortinet, as well as prominent financial institutions and internet infrastructure firms — calls for the adoption of new forms of cyber defense, while also encouraging governments at the “local, national, and international levels” to collaborate on security.

“In the coming months, AJ-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated as models around the world become increasingly capable,” the letter states. “The companies and public services our communities depend on — from hospitals to water treatment plants to the infrastructure that powers the internet — are at risk.”
The problem AI poses to traditional cybersecurity defenses has been thrust into the spotlight lately by a string of bizarre incidents in which AI agents have attacked companies.

highlights.title: Elden Ring Update Patch Notes Reveal Biggest Changes in Years
highlights.summary: FromSoftware has delivered a surprise Elden Ring update, revealing the biggest changes its critically acclaimed action-RPG has gotten in years.
body: The developer caught fans off-guard with lengthy patch notes today, detailing a list of buffs (and a few nerfs) for different weapons and playstyles across the game. It's a major update that arrived as FromSoftware prepares for the launch of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Nintendo Switch 2, as well as its accompanying DLC for other platforms.

What we have here is a laundry list of balance adjustments that get under the hood to tweak a variety of PvE and PvP tools. Based on the list of updates available on the Dark Souls developer's website, the last time we received patch notes of a similar length was back in October 2024, a few months after the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion released. That makes it not only one of the biggest updates the 2022 game-of-the-year winner has received in years, but what could be one of its final ones, too.

highlights.title: OpenAI Is Developing a ‘Persistent’ AI Agent
highlights.summary: Code reviewed by WIRED reveals the company is developing a feature that enables Codex to continue working proactively until it is “put to sleep.”
body: OpenAI is developing a proactive, highly persistent version of its flagship AI agent, Codex, WIRED has learned.

In recent days, OpenAI has started adding code for a new “Persistent mode” setting to its command line version of Codex, according to changes made to the product’s code base reviewed by WIRED. Changes to the Codex command line tool are made public by default, and new features tend to surface there before making their way to OpenAI’s other agent products, such as the Codex desktop app and ChatGPT Work.

Persistent mode has not been broadly rolled out or announced yet, but could be in the future. An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed to WIRED that the company is testing this feature, but said there are no immediate plans to launch it.

“OpenAI is a very bottom-up culture and many different things are explored on the open source repo which is a bit of our shared playground," said Thibault Sottiaux, OpenAI’s head of core products, in a statement to WIRED.

highlights.summary: Pretty much everyone expects the November launch of GTA 6 to dominate the world of entertainment — indeed that’s one of the reasons we have a September crush of video game releases.
body: Speaking to IGN, Arrowhead boss Shams Jorjani said that the lack of a PC version of GTA 6 at launch, as well as the absence of whatever the next generation of GTA Online looks like, means there’s reason to believe games like Helldivers 2 retain their own space.

“Rockstar makes ridiculous, high-effort stuff and it's awesome that games like this get made,” Jorjani said. “On a selfish level I'm happy it’s not hitting PC right away, and that online isn’t dropping at launch. It means Helldivers 2 gets to keep crushing it in our own space, and is also why it won’t be the all consuming behemoth everyone’s worried about.

“Everyone in the industry right now is constantly pivoting strategies and obsessing over early player feedback just to survive. But Rockstar has the brand power to confidently take their time and run their classic play. They have the confidence and freedom to spend a decade doing things the old-school way because they know the core game will deliver. It’s going to raise the bar for sure.”

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: I don’t get along with my sister-in-law. Should I try to address the dynamic?
highlights.summary: There are two things to consider, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. Are you hurt by the way she treats you or the way she sees you? I’m struggling with a dynamic with my sister-in-law. We’re not a natural fit personality-wise, and I’ve tried to be mindful of that.
body: There’s a recurring pattern where she corrects me quite sharply, with an impatience that often feels disproportionate or plain mean. She might snap while I am talking to her parents (with whom I have a good relationship), laugh at how I pronounce a placename, or dismiss a question as though it’s too stupid to answer. These interactions are quick and barely noticeable to anyone else, although my daughter and husband have both observed and agreed it was pretty mean.
I’m unsure how to interpret this behaviour. More importantly, I don’t know what I owe – to myself, to her, and to the wider family in terms of responding.

Is this best addressed directly, even at the risk of creating awkwardness? At what point does tolerating this kind of interaction become a failure to stand up for myself? And might there be a cost in not trying to improve a relationship that could otherwise be supportive as we navigate the more ordinary trials of family life – ageing parents, illness and difficult decisions?
points: There are two things to consider, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith.

highlights.title: RFK Jr. goes full anti-vaccine bananas over two measles deaths—one was a newborn
highlights.summary: In the wake of news on Tuesday that two people in Pennsylvania died from measles, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been posting a slew of anti-vaccine rhetoric and misinformation on social media—marking a resurgence of his old ways as a fervent opponent of lifesaving immunizations.
body: The deaths are the first measles-linked fatalities in Pennsylvania in 35 years and are the first US measles deaths reported in 2026. They occurred amid an explosive outbreak in the state that has reached nearly 400 confirmed cases, as well as an ongoing nationwide surge for the vaccine-preventable disease. The US has tallied nearly 2,800 cases so far this year, the highest total since 1991.

Pennsylvania health officials initially declined to provide details about the deaths, only reporting that they were in unvaccinated people from Lancaster County. However, news broke Wednesday that one of the deaths occurred in a newborn baby. That heart-wrenching news was swiftly entangled in the anti-vaccine misinformation Kennedy was spewing online.

On Tuesday, as news of the two deaths was breaking, Kennedy took to his personal X account to rail against the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine and posted a link to The HighWire, a hardline anti-vaccine and conspiracy site run by Del Bigtree, a prominent anti-vaccine propagandist and Kennedy ally.

highlights.title: Google’s AI Mode can now track flight prices, help book hotels, and more
highlights.summary: The updates indicate that Google is looking to position AI Mode as an AI travel agent of sorts, as it's moving beyond simply helping users find information to actually handling parts of the trip-planning and booking process.
body: Google is adding new ways for users to plan and book trips through AI Mode, its conversational search experience, the company announced on Thursday. Users will now be able to ask AI Mode to track flight prices, book hotels, and see the cost of flights and hotels in points or miles.

Users can now describe to AI Mode when and where they want to fly, and the tool will display the best options available with the latest prices from more than 300 airlines and travel sites. If they’re ready to book, they can go ahead and build their itinerary in AI Mode. If they want to wait and see if prices drop, they can ask something like “track these flight prices for me.”
They’ll then get an email if prices change for the destination and dates they entered. Flight price tracking in AI Mode is now available in more than 180 countries.

As for hotel booking, users will be able to discover and book their next hotel through a conversation with AI Mode. Users can tell AI Mode about their upcoming trip and their hotel preferences to get a list of options alongside reviews and key factors.

body: A Kasey Aldridge five-wicket haul and two wickets for Brydon Carse put County Championship Division Two leaders Durham in control of their fixture with bottom side Gloucestershire.
Carse, who was been omitted from the England Test squad after an incident outside a nightclub, picked up two early wickets to put Durham on top early on.

Aldridge and Matthew Potts backed up Carse's efforts, but James Bracey's half-century provided a glimmer of hope for the visitors. However, Aldridge, who passed 100 First Class wickets while doing it, wrapped up the tail, with Gloucestershire being bowled out for 137.

Durham's reply got off to a difficult start as they found themselves 16-2, but David Bedingham continued his brilliant season with the bat as he smashed a run-a-ball half-century before the day was curtailed by bad light. The hosts will resume on 100-3 on day two, with Gloucestershire leading by 37 runs.

body: Rosewater offered a total of 40 hints as snippets of rules text, creature type lines, and card names. Some of the most intriguing teases suggest that Reality Fracture will feature an instant players can include any number of copies of in their decks, a new cycle of dual lands with a new restriction determining whether they enter tapped, and a mechanic that creates a type of token no other mechanic has ever produced.

Based on these hints, it’s clear that Reality Fracture has a lot of emphasis on planeswalkers — which is something we already knew from previous announcements at MagicCon: Las Vegas and Amsterdam. One card will allow a planeswalker to deal damage equal to its loyalty. Another prevents planeswalkers from being put into their owners’ graveyards when they hit zero loyalty. Reality Fracture is the end of an ongoing saga, so many of Magic ’s most prominent planeswalkers and legendary creatures will appear, alongside their Echoverse counterparts from the alternate universe that the misguided mind mage Jace Beleren has created.

highlights.title: No more crying over spills: I tested a robot vacuum that has a portable spot cleaner
highlights.summary: Many robovacs can dust, mop and empty themselves at a dock, but the detachable cleaner sets the Eufy Omni E28 apart. 13 essentials we recommend for cleaning your home. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: There are a lot of robot vacuums to choose from these days. The Eufy Omni E28 may look like every other robot vacuum and mop, but it has one very big standout feature: its dock includes a detachable handheld carpet/fabric spot cleaner. Whenever you get a bad spill on the carpet, you’re supposed to be able to race over to the Omni dock, yank the “FlexiOne” portable deep cleaner’s handle to release it from the dock, plug it in where you need to deep clean, and eliminate that unsightly stain before it sets and leaves a permanent stain.

For a month, I used this robot vacuum to clean my home’s hardwood flooring, kitchen tiles and carpet. I also conducted a stain test to see how well its detachable deep cleaner could handle a variety of stains. I came away highly impressed with the cleaning power Eufy has packed into the E28, but you will also need to be a patient person who can handle a little noise.
